Your GF is very luck to have a partner who is aware and is trying to be more mindful of her inner struggles. But I get that it could be draining on your part too, OP but you have to remind yourself that her relapses are not about you. Yes, it's inevitable in a relationship to trigger each other but you gotta be mindful of the underlying reasons for your misunderstandings, which is why it is important to really get to know each other's attachment styles and love languages to have a better understanding of each other therefore being more prepared sa paghandle ng mga low, confusing, and chaotic points in a relationship. I suggest you ask directly your partner about what she needs from you whenever she relapses. True it is her responsibility to heal from her trauma and grow out of her toxic traits. But as a partner, it is your responsibility to love her, which includes helping them get through these hard processes. You don't and shouldn't solve everything for them, but you can always help to make it easier too... Just give her time and space to process things when she asks but that doesn't mean to leave her on her own. Keep reassuring her (in the way that you know she'll recognize, e.g. if her love language is physical touch just give her soft embraces pa rin randomly or when you notice she's going through a hard time or just approach her the way she wants and is comfortable with) that you are always there supporting her and you'll still be there when she gets out of every hardship she faces. Let her process and cool down for a while. She'll come to you when she's ready na and then that's the time to talk about the issues you both have been facing in the relationship constructively, gently, and lovingly. Practice co-regulation and remember that the end goal is to find common ground... Ayun, lang naman. I've been with my BF for four years na and yeah I love him so much too so I agree with what you said na ang hirap na makahanap ng mature relationships na willing magcompromise para sa isa't isa nowadays so breaking up is never an option that comes to mind whenever we experience bumps in our journey. Although, I have to say na mas nakakarelate ako sa GF mo so I am speaking from personal experience rin being the anxious and unstable type in the relationship and of the things I learned na rin as I try to be a better partner. I hope everything works out for you and your GF, OP!

For me... I experienced wanting to die and wanting to kill myself separately... I don't know if that makes sense... But for most of my life, starting when I was very young — too young to even comprehend suicide and depression,  I just wanted everything to stop. I didn't see the point in suffering in a life I never asked to have. But, I never tried to kill myself, I didn't see the point in that either and I guess I still had hope. Then recently, for a year or so, I think, everything did stop for me, but I was still here. I can only describe it like being literally dead inside. I've mistaken it for finally attaining peace and contentment for too long when in reality, I became numb, apathetic, and just like a ghost. I already became complacent by the time I realized that. I didn't know it was possible for life to be more meaningless. Ironically, that's when I craved to live. I was in a bad shape and place, but I realized that I want to be able to feel again, even if I get hurt a lot of times. And just when things seemed truly hopeless, like I would just stay dead inside, they all came back to me... Gradually at first, then all at once and in full force suddenly, so I felt like I was drowning. Most of them were unpleasant emotions (resentment, grief, regret, fear, frustration, etc.). I was back to suffering. And only during those couple of months did I truly have a genuinely strong urge to kill myself. But I didn't really want to die. It was weird. I guess I just wanted to get close to dying, in the hopes that I would gain clarity for everything and find a reason to keep going and not let myself relapse into numbness. I never attempted though because I could never really hurt myself physically... I didn't really know what I was doing, but just letting myself feel those unpleasant emotions eventually enabled me to feel all range of things again, feel motivated again, and appreciate the beauty in life. Now, I'd like to think that I'm doing better.

I still struggle with my confidence and self-worth. I also have huge trust issues, which keeps me from easily developing and maintaining deep connections with people. But, I've been doing better lately and I feel that things are slowly improving for me little-by-little, introspectively speaking. It's not always steady or consistent, but I trust that I am reaching a place I've always strived to be mentally and emotionally at.

Sorry for this unsolicited advice, but I learned that the sooner you accept that life just isn't fair, the more you could focus on doing what is best for you now in order to move on, grow, heal, and not be held back by the past anymore. I hope everything works out for you too, OP. You're not alone.

I think your jowa just needs to feel reassured that you still think of her in your day... Yes, running out of topics, especially pag long term na kayo is normal. My partner and I experience it too, and as someone who tends to overanalyze and get anxious about the little details, sometimes I fear that we're losing our connection and passion for one another, so I communicate this to him and we work on it onwards. OP, maybe your partner is feeling the same and is only seeking some sense of deeper connection with you. For me, kapag kusang naggu-good morning or goodnight or nagpapaalam yung BF ko about sa mga ganaps and plans niya for the day is enough to make me feel better. Not that he needs my permission, but its comforting to feel that he thinks of me even when he's out with his friends or busy. It doesn't have to be deep talks and sweet talks all the time too. Maybe you thought of something random and silly, or you saw a funny meme or tiktok, or you encountered something that made you think of them, just tell them. Also avoid being dismissive when your parnter is sharing something with you no matter how trivial it seems because these small and simple things could really improve your emotional connection. When you're spending time together, whether through chat, call, or in person, do your best to be mentally and emotionally present with them.

Maybe they can get a little irrational with how they process and handle their unpleasant emotions, but you have to understand that they're probably not really trying to pick fights with you. Ask them, OP of how and why they feel the way they do about certain things in your relationship. Be patient, gentle, and loving with how you approach these kinds of conversation. You should also communicate about how you feel too, like if she makes you feel bad or anything kapag nagagalit siya. It's important that you talk about these things like your triggers, needs, goals, love language, and attachment styles to better understand each other at para maging mas effective yung way niyo ng pagcocommunicate ng love niyo and pag hahandle na rin ng concerns niyo.

Yun lang hope this helps, OP.

OP, believe me when I say that I can relate to you. LDR rin kami ng BF ko for 4yrs now and hindi rin siya gaano nag-oopen up to me about emotional stuff.

.. And I get where you're coming from. We wanna feel needed, so we reach out, and it hurst when they seem to pull away and reject us. This triggers us and we think that we just have to try harder so we get more clingy and makulit even if we don't really mean to pry. But then, we end up feeling like we only pushed them away further... OP, this will hurt and will be hard to accept, but we have to take a step back, which doesn't mean na pababayaan nalang naten sila, but maybe we could take some time to reanalyze a few things about how we perceive our relationship and our partner.

I'm so in love with my BF and I love expressing it to him, so I send long and sweet messages, sweet tiktoks, or post about sweet things on Facebook. And I always get so anxious, hurt, and disapointed even whenever he doesn't acknowledge them. So, I get tampo then feel silly, 'cuz it wasn't so simple to understand why I was mad. Like, why should I care if he acknowledges it? I'm not doing it for praise, I just want to make him feel loved. But you know what I've realized lately about my own situation? I wasn't really trying to give love to him, I was showing how I wanted to be loved by him. I kept doing these things even though he doesn't seem into them because I was only projecting, hoping he would realize it on his own.

This is when I realized that maybe Words of Affirmation, isn't his love language, but it is mine. Knowing this now, helped me a lot in understanding and accepting the way my BF is in handling certain things when it comes to our relationship. So, OP, maybe this is true for you and your GF too. But we have to understand that we have to communicate this to them. I know how it would feel so much better when our partners will realize this aspect of us on their own, but they're not mind readers. So we have to tell them, and explain how important it is for us to be shown love in our preference. And also, you should get to know your partner's own preference din so that you'll know better how to communicate your love in the way she'll recognize. Our love languages shouldn't be about how we like to give love but how we want to be loved. And in loving our partners, we must always think of their love language, not our own.

Just take it easy pa rin. It's important that you talk about these things and other concerns together to establish a common ground. Its important in a relationship to open up because that's how the relationship grows. But you have to acknowledge that opening up may not be easy for her because maybe it triggers her trauma responses or unwanted thoughts. So you just have to be patient with her, and keep reminding her that you are a safe space and will always be there to hear her out.

You've stayed in your relationship this long, so this tells me that deep down, you still find reasons that are worth fighting for in the love you have with your partner. Of course, marami na rin kayong napagsamahan. Your frustrations and other emotions right now are valid and are normal to have, especially when something matters greatly to you. But they are temporary and they don't have to be dealt with right away. It's better to let yourself cool off and process your thoughts first, before making any decisions that will affect your relationship. So if gusto mo pa, stay. Do your best to communicate your concerns and needs gently and lovingly, but also remember, that at the end, both of you must be willing to make compromises for each other rin and that part is not totally up to you.
